title: IBM Research Automates QEC Decoder Chip Design Using Open AI Agent Factories at 11.5x Lower Inference Cost
key_facts: IBM Research paper using AI agent factories for high-level synthesis chip design
Target: hardware for the Relay-BP decoder for the [[144,12,12]] bivariate bicycle qLDPC code
11.5x lower AI inference cost using open-weight models
One coordinator model with four parallel worker agents
Open-source llm-d serving, 98% prefix-cache hit rate, about $0.11 per million tokens
52x speedup for $26 in the all-open setup
quote_evidence: IBM Research have demonstrated the use of AI agent factories to automate the architectural design of specialized classical hardware for Quantum Error Correction (QEC) decoders, achieving up to a 204x hardware speedup while cutting AI inference costs by 11.5x using open-weight models.
This allowed the all-open agent factory to deliver a 52x hardware speedup for $26 in inference cost.
why_it_matters_hint: AI agents on open models may make designing quantum decoder chips cheap enough to be practical.
notes: Read Quantum Computing Report article via curl (fulltext file was empty). Paper not read directly. Authors named in the article include Abhishek Bhandwaldar, Mihir Choudhury and Ruchir Puri; roles not stated, so not named in the entry.
